question.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the absolute value on the left side of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}2|5x-3|+1 & =15 \\ 2|5x-3| & =14 \\ |5x-3| & =7\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the following two cases:

- If $|5x-3|=5x-3,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|5x-3| & =7 \\ 5x-3 & =7 \\ 5x & =10 \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

- If $|5x-3|=-(5x-3),$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|5x-3| & =7 \\ -(5x-3) & =7 \\ -5x+3 & =7 \\ -5x & =4 \\ x & =-\frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=-\frac{4}{5}$ and $x=2.$
